Uses withLock and inFlightCreate dedup, but inFlightCreate is not itself guarded by the lock during assignment; two rapid calls could both see null and each create a separate Promise that the lock still serializes. Could be tighter.
No cached data reused across awaits except DB handle, which is opened once. n/a

Clean separation between web and native backends; only minor quibble is web/native branches are selected by Platform.OS inline rather than via a pluggable backend interface.
Single file does many things: public API, native backend, web backend, mutex, base64 helpers, validation. Could be split into smaller modules.
Likely eslint-clean, but uses catch (_) which many linters flag.
Imports are minimal and grouped. n/a

AES-GCM IV is fresh per encryption via getRandomValues; no nonce reuse risk. n/a
No WebView or iframe usage. n/a

Provides zeroize() and clears many Uint8Arrays, but the native base64 string copy and intermediate Array.from ciphertext/iv arrays cannot be zeroized; JS strings are immutable. Residual exposure remains.
SecureStore is statically imported and asserted via isAvailableAsync() before use, but the static import still assumes the module is present in the bundle. Good but not perfect for OTA boundaries.
Calls SecureStore.isAvailableAsync() before every native operation; still relies on the module being present at import time.
Errors are wrapped and re-thrown as KeyStorageError; callers receive them. Could include structured error codes for programmatic handling.
Failures are thrown to caller; no retry/backoff for transient storage failures, but arguably storage failures are not transient.

createAndStoreSeed throws on failure and wipes partial state, which is correct. Minor: nested cleanup error is swallowed with catch (_).
inFlightCreate dedups concurrent create calls, but loadSeed, wipeAllKeychainData and other operations are not deduped; concurrent load+wipe could race.
No timeout/retry logic in this module. n/a
No retry logic. n/a

catch (_) { // ignore nested cleanup errors } on line ~273 is a silent catch block; it swallows a real cleanup failure with only a comment. Static rule ERR-001 already caught it, and this LLM rule confirms it is contextually silent.

Crypto and security model are documented in the header, but the failure-path cleanup reasoning could use an inline comment at the silent catch.
